findings.title: Northwind Retail Group — Change-of-Control Consent Requirement and Imminent Renewal Risk
findings.what_would_raise_confidence: Executed consent letter from Northwind confirming approval of the change of control. Executed renewal agreement for the post-June 2026 period. Absence of any executed amendments modifying Sections 14.2 or 14.3.
findings.ev_method: ARR at risk × contribution margin assumption (0.40) × loss probability assumption (0.35) × entry multiple (12.0). Contribution margin and loss probability are deal-team assumptions, not observed facts.
findings.finding: The executed Northwind MSA (CTR-00001, Section 14.2) treats a change of control of Harborline as an assignment requiring Northwind's prior written consent; if the transaction completes without that consent, Northwind may terminate on 90 days' notice within 180 days of awareness (Section 14.3). The contract also expires on 30 June 2026 with no automatic renewal, requiring a bilateral written renewal executed at least 90 days before expiry — meaning the renewal window opens on or before 31 March 2026, coinciding with the expected close date. Management's CIM and contract summary both incorrectly state no change-of-control restriction exists, and the Board's own General Counsel confirmed the restriction in October 2025 board minutes. Northwind represents the single largest customer at 27.28% of closing ARR ($10.55M), making this the highest-concentration risk in the portfolio.

evidence.section: Section 14.2 Assignment and Change of Control
evidence.quote: For the avoidance of doubt, a Change of Control of Supplier shall constitute an assignment for the purposes of this Section 14.2.
Customer may terminate this Agreement on ninety (90) days' written notice given at any time within one hundred and eighty (180) days of becoming aware of such Change of Control.
There shall be no automatic renewal. Any renewal shall be by written agreement of both parties executed not less than ninety (90) days prior to expiry.
Section 14.2 treats a change of control of the Company as an assignment requiring Northwind's prior written consent.
None noted [change of control restriction]
All customer contracts are freely assignable on a change of control.

findings.mitigation: Initiate consent outreach to Northwind immediately upon signing of any LOI or SPA. Simultaneously commence renewal negotiations to secure a signed renewal agreement before the 31 March 2026 deadline. Engage Northwind's executive sponsor at board level. Prepare a retention plan addressing any commercial concerns Northwind may raise in connection with the ownership change.
findings.spa_protection: Consider with transaction counsel: (1) a condition precedent to closing requiring receipt of Northwind's written consent to the change of control; (2) a specific indemnity covering losses arising from Northwind's exercise of its Section 14.3 termination right; (3) a purchase-price adjustment or escrow holdback sized to the Northwind ARR exposure if consent is not obtained pre-close; (4) a seller covenant requiring management to use best efforts to obtain consent and execute a renewal agreement prior to closing; (5) a representation and warranty that no counterparty has indicated an intention to exercise termination rights.

findings.title: Recurring Legal Settlement Misclassified as Non-Recurring EBITDA Add-Back (ADJ-003)
findings.what_would_raise_confidence: Settlement agreement documents for FY2023, FY2024, and FY2025 confirming separate counterparties and fully concluded distinct legal matters. Absence of any FY2026 settlement provision in audited accounts. Legal counsel opinion confirming the series is fully resolved with no further exposure.
findings.ev_method: Rejected EBITDA amount ($2,100,000) × entry multiple (12.0). Agent 5 verdict: Rejected. No contribution margin or loss probability applied; this is an EBITDA-method finding.
findings.finding: Management has added back $2.1M in each of FY2023, FY2024, and FY2025 under the label 'One-time legal settlement — non-recurring.' Board minutes from October 2025 (Item 7) explicitly describe 'the third annual settlement under the ongoing series of commercial disputes with former channel partners' at $2.1M, consistent with the prior two years, and the Board itself asked whether provision should be made for a further FY2026 settlement. This contemporaneous board-level characterisation directly contradicts management's non-recurring classification. Agent 5 rejected ADJ-003 in full, reducing Team Adjusted EBITDA by $2.1M. At the deal entry multiple of 12x, the misclassification implies a $25.2M overstatement of Enterprise Value relative to a correctly normalised EBITDA base.

evidence.quote: The CFO reported that the third annual settlement under the ongoing series of commercial disputes with former channel partners had been concluded at $2.1M, consistent with the prior two years. The Board asked whether provision should be made for a further settlement in FY2026.
One-time legal settlement | 2,100,000 | Settlement of a commercial dispute. Non-recurring.

findings.mitigation: Obtain all three settlement agreements (FY2023, FY2024, FY2025) to assess whether counterparties and legal matters are genuinely distinct and fully concluded. Obtain legal counsel opinion on the probability of a FY2026 settlement. If the series is confirmed as recurring, the EBITDA base must be restated and the purchase price renegotiated accordingly. Request management to provide a FY2026 budget that either provisions for or explicitly excludes further settlements.
findings.spa_protection: Consider with transaction counsel: (1) a specific indemnity covering any FY2026 or subsequent settlement payments arising from the same series of channel-partner disputes; (2) a representation and warranty that the FY2025 settlement is the final payment in the series and no further claims are outstanding; (3) an escrow or holdback sized to at least one year's settlement amount ($2.1M) pending confirmation of no FY2026 settlement; (4) a purchase-price adjustment mechanism tied to the EBITDA impact if a further settlement is paid within 24 months post-close.

findings.title: Vantage Grocers — SLA Breach Pattern, Contractual Termination Right, and MFN Exposure
findings.what_would_raise_confidence: Monthly availability logs confirming whether the 99.0% consecutive-month threshold was breached. Formal escalation notices exchanged under Section 12.3. Confirmation of whether Vantage has served or threatened a termination notice. Legal analysis of MFN credit exposure quantum. Full amendment set for CTR-00002.
findings.ev_method: ARR at risk × contribution margin assumption (0.40) × loss probability assumption (0.35) × entry multiple (12.0). Contribution margin and loss probability are deal-team assumptions, not observed facts. MFN credit exposure is separately unquantified due to absence of a defensible credit calculation methodology in available evidence.
findings.finding: Vantage Grocers (CTR-00002, $4.68M closing ARR, 12.11% of total) presents three compounding risks: (1) Support ticket data shows 6 Severity 1 incidents in the worst rolling three-month window (April–June 2025), exceeding the contractual threshold of 4 that activates Section 12.3 escalation and makes Section 12.2 termination remedies available; CSAT scores have deteriorated from 2.7 in Q2 2025 to 1.8 in Q4 2025; board minutes confirm the customer's executive sponsor has invoked the escalation provision and placed the FY2027 renewal 'under active review.' (2) The executed MSA contains a most-favoured-customer pricing clause (Section 8.4) requiring Vantage's 18% discount to remain no less favourable than discounts granted to comparable-spend customers; Pinnacle Outdoor (CTR-00003) received a 34% discount in March 2025 and qualifies as comparable under the 50%-of-ACV threshold in Section 8.5, creating a retrospective credit obligation that management has not quantified. (3) Management's CIM and contract summary both incorrectly state no MFN exists. The Board's General Counsel flagged the MFN issue in October 2025 with no documented resolution.

is and shall remain not less favourable than the effective discount granted by Supplier to any other customer of comparable annual committed spend.

continued service instability at Vantage Grocers, with Severity 1 incident volumes elevated since April and customer satisfaction scores at their lowest recorded level for the account. The customer's executive sponsor has invoked the escalation provision of the MSA and has placed the FY2027 renewal 'under active review'.
The General Counsel asked that the Vantage most-favoured-customer provision be reviewed in light of this.

findings.title: Pro-Forma Unactioned Cost Savings Included in Historical EBITDA (ADJ-005)
findings.what_would_raise_confidence: Board resolution approving the restructuring programme. Redundancy notices served to affected employees. Signed settlement agreements with affected employees. Audited FY2026 accounts confirming the saving was realised.
findings.ev_method: Rejected EBITDA amount ($1,400,000) × entry multiple (12.0). Agent 5 verdict: Rejected. No contribution margin or loss probability applied; this is an EBITDA-method finding.
findings.finding: Management's QoE schedule includes a $1.4M add-back (ADJ-005) for a planned headcount reduction of 14 FTE, explicitly acknowledging that 'no notice has yet been served' and the reduction is 'scheduled for Q1 FY2026.' This is a prospective, unactioned cost saving that has not been realised in the FY2025 analysis period; the cost was incurred in FY2025 and the saving belongs to a future period. No board resolution, restructuring plan, or redundancy notice is evidenced in the data room. Agent 5 rejected ADJ-005 in full. At the deal entry multiple of 12x, inclusion of this item implies a $16.8M overstatement of Enterprise Value.

findings.title: Pro-Forma New Logo Annualisation Included in Historical EBITDA (ADJ-010)
findings.what_would_raise_confidence: Executed contracts for all new FY2025 logos confirming contracted ACV/ARR. Invoices covering a full 12-month period for each new logo. Management's annualisation methodology and workings showing how $1,650,000 was derived from specific customer contracts.
findings.ev_method: Rejected EBITDA amount ($1,650,000) × entry multiple (12.0). Agent 5 verdict: Rejected. No contribution margin or loss probability applied; this is an EBITDA-method finding.
findings.finding: Management's QoE schedule includes a $1.65M add-back (ADJ-010) representing the annualised full-year contribution of new logos won during FY2025. SQL analysis identifies 20 new customers with first_order_date in FY2025 generating $1,878,956 in actual FY2025 revenue — already captured in reported EBITDA. The $1.65M adjustment adds prospective revenue not earned in FY2025 to the historical EBITDA base. Cascade Foods Holdings (CUST-0006) accounts for 64% of new logo revenue ($1,206,022) with only 3 invoices, making annualisation highly assumption-dependent. No executed contracts for the remaining new logos are in the data room to confirm contracted ARR. Agent 5 rejected ADJ-010 in full. At the deal entry multiple of 12x, this implies a $19.8M overstatement of Enterprise Value.

findings.title: Atlas Distribution Exclusivity Blocks CIM European Direct Expansion Growth Plan
findings.what_would_raise_confidence: A signed waiver, amendment, or termination of the Atlas exclusivity covenant. Confirmation that existing direct customers in the territory were onboarded before the exclusivity effective date or under a permitted exception. Legal analysis of whether any existing direct territory customers constitute a breach of the exclusivity covenant.
findings.ev_method: ARR at risk (Atlas ARR + direct territory ARR per CF-005: $1,830,725.38) × contribution margin assumption (0.40) × loss probability assumption (0.35) × entry multiple (12.0). The $6M ARR growth plan (CLM-07) is a forecast and cannot be priced as lost ARR under the stated methodology; only current ARR at risk from the exclusivity constraint is priced. Contribution margin and loss probability are deal-team assumptions, not observed facts.
findings.finding: The CIM's primary growth thesis is direct European expansion worth $6M ARR by FY2028 (CLM-07, Contradicted). The executed Atlas Distribution reseller agreement (CTR-00004, Section 4.3) prohibits Harborline from directly or indirectly marketing, licensing, selling, or delivering the platform to any customer in the EU, UK, Switzerland, or Norway through 31 December 2029 — beyond the expected close date. The exclusivity survives assignment and binds any successor in interest (Section 22.1). SQL data shows 41 direct customers in the territory, 10 of whom started after the exclusivity effective date (January 2024), raising a potential breach question. The board itself asked in October 2025 whether the Atlas arrangement permits direct European sales, with management undertaking to revert — with no documented resolution. The IT overview confirms no EU data residency capability exists, adding a further implementation barrier to the growth plan.

evidence.quote: Supplier shall not, whether directly or through any affiliate, agent, or other reseller, market, license, sell, or deliver the Platform to any customer whose principal place of business is within the Territory, nor solicit any such customer.
Exclusivity survives any assignment and binds any successor in interest.
Direct expansion into Europe is the primary growth vector, worth $6M ARR by FY2028.
A director asked whether the Atlas Distribution arrangement permits direct sales in Europe. Management undertook to revert.
No EU data residency capability exists today.

findings.spa_protection: Consider with transaction counsel: (1) a specific indemnity covering any breach-of-exclusivity claims by Atlas arising from direct territory customers onboarded after January 2024; (2) a condition precedent or closing deliverable requiring management to obtain Atlas's written confirmation of the scope of permitted direct sales; (3) a purchase-price adjustment or earn-out reduction if the European growth plan cannot be executed as presented in the CIM; (4) a representation and warranty that no breach of the Atlas exclusivity covenant has occurred.

findings.title: Cascade Foods Holdings Misclassified as New Logo — Re-engagement After Churn
findings.what_would_raise_confidence: CRM new-logo definition policy confirming whether entity-level or group-level classification applies. Prior 2021 agreement file and billing history for the Cascade Foods operating subsidiary (CUST-0005). Confirmation of whether the $1,629,016 ARR is included in management's NRR and logo churn calculations.
findings.ev_method: No EV impact calculated. This is a data/representation finding. The misclassification affects NRR and logo churn metrics (CLM-02, CLM-04) but does not independently support a defensible ARR-risk or EBITDA-method pricing calculation beyond what is already captured in RF-003 (NRR/churn) and RF-005 (new logo annualisation).
findings.finding: Management's contract summary labels Cascade Foods Holdings (CUST-0006, $1.63M closing ARR) as a 'New logo win FY2025.' The executed MSA (CTR-00006, Recital B) states the customer was previously party to a 2021 MSA through its operating subsidiary Cascade Foods (CUST-0005), which expired on 28 February 2025 and was not renewed. Subscription data confirms CUST-0005 was active at $1.63M ARR in February 2025 and churned in March 2025, with CUST-0006 re-engaging in June 2025. The re-engagement was secured only after a competitive re-evaluation and required a discount increase from 15% to 21% plus a $180,000 onboarding credit. Classifying this as a new logo inflates the NRR and logo churn metrics and may overstate the quality of the retention profile presented in the CIM.

evidence.quote: Customer was previously party to a Master Services Agreement with Supplier dated 1 March 2021 (the 'Prior Agreement') in the name of its operating subsidiary Cascade Foods, which Prior Agreement expired on 28 February 2025 and was not renewed at that time.

Discount of twenty-one per cent (21%) against list, an increase from the fifteen per cent (15%) applied under the Prior Agreement, reflecting the interruption in service and Customer's re-tendering of the requirement.
New logo win FY2025

findings.mitigation: Require management to restate NRR, GRR, and logo churn metrics treating CUST-0005 and CUST-0006 as the same economic group. Obtain the prior 2021 agreement and billing history to confirm the full relationship timeline. Assess whether the $180,000 onboarding credit and increased discount represent a structural pricing concession that affects the quality of the re-engaged ARR.
findings.spa_protection: Consider with transaction counsel: (1) a representation and warranty that the NRR, GRR, and logo churn metrics in the CIM are calculated on a consistent basis and that the Cascade re-engagement is correctly classified; (2) a specific indemnity covering any credit or discount obligations arising from the Cascade re-engagement terms that were not disclosed in the data room.

findings.title: Customer Concentration Materially Understated — Northwind at 27.4% vs Claimed <10%
findings.what_would_raise_confidence: Executed customer-group mapping amendments if additional parent relationships exist beyond dim_customer.parent_customer_id. A documented revenue concentration policy confirming the basis of the CIM claim.
findings.ev_method: No EV impact calculated. This is a data/representation finding. The concentration risk is already captured in RF-001 (Northwind ARR at risk). Pricing the concentration separately would double-count the same underlying economic exposure.
findings.finding: The CIM states 'no single customer accounts for more than 10% of revenue' (CLM-01, Contradicted). SQL analysis of FY2025 invoice data shows Northwind Retail Group (CUST-0001) generated $11,723,657 in FY2025 revenue, representing 27.44% of total FY2025 revenue — 17.4 percentage points above the claimed threshold. The group-level analysis produces the same result. This misrepresentation materially understates single-customer concentration risk and, combined with the change-of-control consent requirement (RF-001), means the largest customer relationship is both more concentrated and more contractually constrained than disclosed.

evidence.quote: no single customer accounts for more than 10% of revenue

evidence.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT i.customer_id AS k, SUM(l.line_amount_usd) AS rev FROM workspace.aava_deal_studio.fact_invoice_line l JOIN workspace.aava_deal_studio.fact_invoice i ON l.invoice_id = i.invoice_id WHERE year(to_date(i.invoice_date)) = 2025 GROUP BY 1) SELECT k AS top_customer_id, ROUND(rev,2) AS top_customer_revenue, ROUND(100 * rev / SUM(rev) OVER(), 2) AS top1_pct FROM r QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC, k)=1

findings.mitigation: Restate the CIM concentration disclosure to reflect actual Northwind revenue share. Assess whether any other customers approach or exceed the 10% threshold. Incorporate the correct concentration data into the investment thesis and underwriting model. Prioritise Northwind consent and renewal actions (see RF-001) given the elevated concentration.
findings.spa_protection: Consider with transaction counsel: (1) a representation and warranty that the customer concentration disclosures in the CIM are accurate as of the signing date; (2) a specific indemnity covering losses arising from any material misrepresentation of customer concentration in the CIM.

overlap_groups.description: Northwind change-of-control, concentration, and CLM-08 claim all relate to the same CUST-0001 economic exposure. ARR at risk ($10,547,040.61) and EV impact are counted once in RF-001. RF-008 (concentration) carries null EV impact to avoid double-counting.

Vantage SLA/MFN risk (RF-003), Cascade re-engagement (RF-007), and NRR/logo churn overstatement (CLM-02, CLM-04) all relate to retention quality. RF-003 prices the Vantage ARR at risk. RF-007 carries null EV impact as the Cascade ARR is not independently at risk beyond what is captured in the retention metrics. NRR/churn overstatement is a data finding with no separate ARR-risk pricing.
EBITDA overstatement findings RF-002, RF-004, RF-005 each relate to distinct rejected adjustments (ADJ-003, ADJ-005, ADJ-010) with separate economic bases. No overlap; each is priced independently.

deduplication.method: Economic exposure identified per underlying customer/contract/adjustment. Where the same ARR or EBITDA amount would be counted by multiple findings, it is priced in the finding with the most direct contractual or earnings evidence and set to null in corroborating findings.

unresolved_items.issue: 10 direct territory customers were onboarded after the Atlas exclusivity effective date (January 2024). unresolved_items.required_evidence: Full customer country normalisation (UK vs United Kingdom mapping). Any Atlas amendments or waivers. Legal analysis of whether the 10 post-exclusivity direct customers constitute a breach.
unresolved_items.pricing_impact: Potential breach liability not quantified. Excluded from aggregate totals pending legal analysis.

The commercial terms of any such re-negotiation are unknown and could result in a pricing concession beyond the ARR-at-risk scenario modelled.
unresolved_items.required_evidence: Northwind's commercial position on consent and any fee re-negotiation demands. Legal analysis of Section 14.4 scope.
unresolved_items.pricing_impact: Potential additional ARR reduction not quantified. Excluded from aggregate totals.

unresolved_items.pricing_impact: Potential additional $2.1M recurring cost not included in aggregate EV impact. If recurring, the correct EBITDA normalisation would treat this as an ongoing cost, further reducing Team Adjusted EBITDA.
